title: Visiting another stream
hook: all are welcome at any gurdwara; courtesy is enough

segments.voice: Yesterday, one Granth for all: every stream bows to the same Guru Granth Sahib. Your line was one granth. What shared center did you name? Day one thousand three hundred fifty-eight.

A shoe rack by the door, already full. A basket of orange and blue head scarves for anyone who came without one. A small trough of water for washing hands. Nobody at the entrance asks which stream you belong to, or whether you're a Sikh at all. Someone may smile and point you toward the scarves. That's the whole admission process. This week has been full of questions Sikhs disagree about. It ends at the door every stream keeps open.
screen: `SHOES OFF, HEAD COVERED, HANDS WASHED.` → `NOBODY ASKS WHICH STREAM.` → `A DOOR KEPT OPEN.`

segments.voice: Look back at the week. Open questions held kindly. The meat question and its different plates. The Dasam Granth and its shared devotion. Women among the five, and a conversation that continues. Many voices and one Guru. One Granth at the front of every room. Here's what makes all of that livable: any Sikh, and anyone else, can walk into a gurdwara of a stream not their own and be welcome. What's asked is courtesy, not agreement. Cover your head. Take off your shoes. Leave tobacco and alcohol outside. Sit on the floor with everyone else, facing the Granth, and don't turn your back to it or point your feet at it. If karah prashad, the warm sweet offering, is handed out, receive it in cupped hands. If you're invited to langar, sit in the row and eat what's served. That's it. No one checks your theology at the door. Gurbani gives a line for this openness. On Ang 671, Guru Arjan says, here in paraphrase, I have made everyone my friend, and I am a friend to all. A Nihang gurdwara may feel different from a Western sangat's, and a Namdhari gathering different again: the dress, the tunes, the pace. A visitor doesn't need to settle any of this week's questions to sit down. Courtesy is enough. Welcome does the rest.
screen: `A WEEK OF OPEN QUESTIONS.` · `COURTESY, NOT AGREEMENT.` · `HEAD, SHOES, FLOOR, CUPPED HANDS.` · `A FRIEND TO ALL.` · then, large: `COURTESY IS ENOUGH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: plan a visit to a different gurdwara. Settle, and breathe. Think of a gurdwara you've never been to, or one whose stream is different from the one you know. If you don't know one, think of any place of worship you've wondered about. Walk through the visit in your mind: the shoes, the head covering, washing your hands, sitting down on the carpet. Notice any nervousness, and let it out with the breath. Then choose a week this month when you could actually go. If you pray, you can ask for an open heart on the way. The bell holds the time.
Visiting another stream. Anyone is welcome at any gurdwara; what's asked is a covered head, bare feet, and courtesy, not agreement. Today's word.

Your line: courtesy is enough. Today, when you enter someone else's space, learn its one or two customs and keep them, without needing to agree with everything there. Day one thousand three hundred fifty-eight.

howItsDone: Gurdwaras of every Sikh stream welcome visitors of any background; guests cover their heads, remove their shoes, leave tobacco and alcohol outside, sit on the floor facing the Guru Granth Sahib, receive karah prashad in cupped hands and may share langar.

notes: Ang 671 'sabh ko meet ham aapan keenaa ham sabhnaa ke saajan' paraphrased as 'I have made everyone my friend, and I am a friend to all'. Please confirm Ang and paraphrase.

Visitor courtesies (head covered, shoes off, hands washed, no tobacco or alcohol, sitting on the floor, not turning the back or pointing feet toward the Granth, karah prashad in cupped hands) are general gurdwara etiquette; please confirm.
Gurdwara glossed as 'the Guru's door': this is the common gloss, not an etymology from a cited text. Keeper may prefer 'the Guru's house'.
Day 1358 is a week end; the teach looks back over 1352–1357.
Orange and blue scarves in the hook are a scene detail, not a claim.
Editor: dropped the 'Guru's door' gloss from the original note (an etymology not in the cited text); no other changes.
